title: Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Began as a GameCube Exclusive
hook: In 2002 an Oregon studio called Pipeworks put 11 monsters on the GameCube and GameSpot called it the best Godzilla game to date. On November 3, Godzilla Day, Atari and Pipeworks brought it back remastered with online play. Which kaiju are you picking first?
script: Did you know the Godzilla game that just got remastered started life as a GameCube exclusive from a small Oregon studio? In October two thousand two, Infogrames, selling under the Atari name, released Godzilla Destroy All Monsters Melee. It was built by Pipeworks, a studio based in Oregon. Godzilla games before it had a rough reputation with critics. GameSpot called this one the best Godzilla game to date. You could pick from eleven monsters, most of them unlocked over time, and smash through cities while fighting each other. The final boss of the adventure mode was Mechagodzilla. An expanded Xbox version followed in April two thousand three with a twelfth monster, Kiryu, the newest Mechagodzilla from the films at the time. Pipeworks went on to make two sequels, Godzilla Save the Earth and then Godzilla Unleashed, and the studio calls them its Godzilla trilogy. The original never came to a PlayStation console. That changed this week. Atari and Pipeworks released a remaster on November third, Godzilla Day, for PlayStation Five, Xbox, Switch Two and PC. It is rebuilt in Unreal Engine Five and adds online play for the first time. Which monster are you picking first? Follow for more gaming history.
